title: A worker verification's test shards run on ready hosts while a merge trial starts
description: A worker's host-run test check over many tests, two ready hosts reached through graphyard-host-shim under a heavy-job cap of one. Its shards run on both hosts as a trial's do, holding no heavy-job slot, so a merge trial takes the one slot at once. Master status's remoteShards shows it, all remote. A one-script check beside a declared Postgres Compose service runs whole on a ready host, which starts the service, runs the script on its network and removes it, else here when no host is ready or drops it; the reason shows by the host's load line in master status and on Workers. host add YOU@HOST prepares a host over SSH and adds it once under any name; a second coordinator joins by host share; one host serves two installs, each key its own release's helper. The loop sends its helper only to a host lacking a verb it speaks, taken when its digest matches; one whose update fails reads away with the reason. A ready host on a helper from before the update verb stays ready; master status says: HOST runs an older helper: run mainworks host add YOU@HOST in a terminal to update it. A host without Docker reads away naming its unit state. The warm image, keyed to main's commit and lockfile, is sent once its database starts, stays on a host a run named within the hour, is re-sent when a host lacks it, reaches ready hosts first, starts the CLI in 0.6 CPU-seconds, rebuilds a head's changed source. While a leftover limit file fixes the budget and a host is ready, master status names it and hostHeavyJobs=auto removes it. A host takes shards while its busy cores plus shards placed there stay under its cores less two; master status shows each host's shards. A trial started in a merge's cycle survives a restart, run once. Builders of every runtime go first to a ready, cool host with room; an older helper's host is skipped, stays ready, status says why; a session that fails before it writes starts here. A trial's e2e cases run on ready hosts on each live helper, a host fault's here.

steps.name: Add a fake host with one command that prepares it over SSH, add it again under another name and see one entry, then let a second coordinator join it by share and run a shard there
Run a worker verification on two fake hosts and start a merge trial beside it
Run a Claude, Codex, OpenCode and Cursor builder on a fake host with its login in memory only, skip a host on an older helper while it stays ready, and run one here only when no host has room
Fail builder preparation on a test machine, start the same attempt here, and pause host sessions for 30 minutes with the reason in status and Workers
Skip a test machine whose helper lacks run-session with its reason in status, and start here a builder session that fails before it writes anything
Land one head, start the waiting head's trial in the same cycle, restart the loop and see the trial adopted and run once
Place shards on hosts by free cores, show each host's shards in master status and raise one line while this machine is overloaded beside a half-free host
Show a leftover limit file in master status while hosts are ready, and lift it with hostHeavyJobs=auto
Run a script check and its Postgres service whole on a fake host, and on this machine when the host is away, with the reason in master status and on the Workers page
Run a script check on a fake host whose first heat probe is hot and second cool, and on this machine with both values when it stays hot, on a fake clock
Reach a check's Postgres service by its name on a fake host with no DNS resolver, as a remote shard has none
Run a declared check with a service image built locally on the coordinator (never pushed) and verify it is sent once and answers on the compute host
Read a fake host whose Docker unit is not enabled and one whose unit failed, and show the reason
Prepare one fake host for two installs at different helper releases, probe each through its own helper, and name the older helper in one master status line
Update a fake host's older helper from the loop, send it shards, and refuse a helper with the wrong digest
Build the commit- and lockfile-keyed warm image, verify warm CLI startup under 0.6 CPU-seconds and head source rebuild on a remote host
Discard a warm image whose test database fails to start, naming the failing command, and run the trial on the previous image
Run trial shards on a run-shard:2 helper and a run-shard:3 helper, mark a refusing helper away with its refusal, and link Postgres's libraries in the warm image
Upload three base tips' warm images, then run a check on the first on every live helper version; two installs keep each other's images and an hour-old one is pruned
Run a merge trial's own e2e cases on two fake test machines, its secret's and environment's cases here, a dropped host's case here once, and on each live helper version

Run the daily catalog inside 45 minutes: this machine's cases in lanes dealt by the timing baseline, a test machine's in one shard per six free cores each in its own checkout, and each lane's run adopted after a restart
